headline: Alex Caruso (ankle) is not expected to be out long term
body: After missing this third straight contest on Monday vs. the Cavs, Caruso is expected to not be out long term as his ankle sprain is not deemed serious. Even when the veteran guard gets back into the fold, the Thunder will still rely on the younger guys for heavy minutes.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Oklahoma City Thunder sign Dalen Terry to two-year deal
body: Terry enters his fifth season in the NBA, departing from the Warriors G League team in Santa Cruz. In 218 games played, Terry has averaged 3.5 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists. His most recent stints last season with the Bulls and 76ers, saw him play just 11.5 minutes per game. The 6-7 wing will help provide the Thunder some depth in that position as the injuries have piled up just in the opening weeks of the season.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Darius Garland accumulated 16 points (5-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Raptors.
body: Garland’s efficiency remains an issue for fantasy managers. In addition to the poor shooting, he committed seven turnovers against the Raptors. Four of those turnovers occurred in the fourth quarter, as the Clippers were outscored 47-27 and surrendered a 13-point lead. Some may view this as a good “buy low” opportunity, but Garland has committed at least five turnovers in five of the Clippers’ first seven games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Strus (foot) posted 11 points (3-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Raptors.
body: Nearly a month after injuring his foot during a preseason game, Strus made his Clippers debut on Monday. Unsurprisingly, he was a bit rusty offensively, but Strus made contributions on both ends of the floor. He played 23 minutes, a number that will increase as any restrictions are lifted. Fantasy managers in 12-team leagues can hold off on adding Strus for now, but he may be worth picking up soon.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Jackson finished Monday’s loss to the Raptors with 19 points (9-of-11 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer.
body: Inconsistent as a starter in the Clippers’ first six games, Jackson was moved to the bench on Monday. The decision could have been matchup-based, but Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue stuck with Brook Lopez (12/6/1/1/1 with one three-pointer) as the starting center after Toronto ruled out Jakob Poeltl. Jackson didn’t let the demotion get him down, as he recorded a season-high point total and matched his previous high in rebounds. Simply put, even if Jackson continues to come off the bench, those rostering him shouldn’t throw in the towel.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kobe Sanders produced 26 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Raptors.
body: The Clippers didn’t have Derrick Jones Jr. or Rui Hachimura for Monday’s game, so Sanders made his second start of the season. The second-year wing had the best night of his NBA career, dropping a career-high 26 points. Sanders scored 13 points in both halves, but he may have run out of steam late. Shooting 1-of-5 from the field, Sanders scored five points in the fourth quarter, and the Clippers shot 30.4 percent as a team. That’s how a team goes from leading by 13 to losing by seven.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes accumulated 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 8-of-15 FTs), 15 rebounds, eight assists and two steals in Monday’s win over the Clippers.
body: Barnes appeared to aggravate his sore left hip during the third quarter, but he returned to the game after some time on the bench. And it’s a good thing he did, as the Raptors forward was outstanding in the fourth quarter. Barnes recorded 15 points, eight rebounds, one assist and two steals in the quarter, helping the Raptors erase a 13-point deficit to win by seven. Barnes struggled at the foul line, but that was his only negative on his final stat line.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles amassed 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Clippers.
body: With Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) out for a second straight game, Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic gave Murray-Boyles his first start of the season. The second-year forward capitalized on the opportunity, finishing two points shy of his career high. Add in the rebounds and blocks, and this was a good night for fantasy managers rostering Murray-Boyles. Trayce Jackson-Davis, who was ineffective as a starter on Sunday, played just two minutes against the Clippers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Immanuel Quickley finished Monday’s win over the Clippers with 27 points (8-of-13 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: The Raptors entered the third quarter trailing by 13, but thanks to the tandem of Quickley and Scottie Barnes, they managed to walk down the Clippers and win by seven. Quickley and Barnes scored 29 of Toronto’s 47 points in the quarter, with Quickley providing 14. It’s early, but IQ has been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats, exceeding his Yahoo ADP by a comfortable margin.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: RJ Barrett tallied 26 points (10-of-19 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Clippers.
body: Barrett scored 16 points in the first half of Monday’s game, shooting 7-of-9 from the field. The overall stat line was good, except for one category: free-throw percentage. Barrett is shooting a career-worst 58.8 percent from the charity stripe this season, a number that has done his category league value no favors. That said, Barrett is a career 69.5 percent shooter, so it may not be too surprising that he’s started slowly in that regard.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dillon Brooks amassed 18 points (5-of-8 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Brooks received a technical foul early in the third quarter that may have been more about “reputation” than anything he did in the situation that led to Draymond Green’s ejection. It isn’t a big deal right now, but the Suns getting that technical foul overturned (if they appeal it) would give Brooks a little more room later in the season. As for his performance against the Warriors, “The Villain” didn’t have any defensive stats, but the points, rebounds, assists, three-pointers and percentages were solid.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Miles Bridges accounted for 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Bridges has scored at least 21 points in back-to-back games and shot the ball well on Monday. Compared to his final season with the Hornets, Bridges is averaging more rebounds, steals and blocks, while his scoring average is nearly the same (17.0 compared to 17.1 last season). Some fantasy managers may consider selling high, but Bridges’ current averages are sustainable.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Ja’Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles will start Monday’s game against the Clippers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Christie (hip) will not return to Monday’s game against the Kings.
body: Christie played eight minutes before leaving Monday’s game with a right hip injury. Walter Clayton Jr. replaced him to start the third quarter, and Christie’s absence may also free up minutes for Marcus Sasser.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (hip) is available for Monday’s game against the Clippers while Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is out.
body: While Barnes is good to go after initially being questionable, Poeltl will miss a second straight game. Trayce Jackson-Davis started Sunday’s loss to the Lakers but wasn’t productive enough to merit streaming in any fantasy league.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is now doubtful for Monday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Poeltl did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, with Trayce Jackson-Davis replacing him in the starting lineup. TJD offered little value in that role, however, so there’s no need to consider streaming him if Poeltl remains out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (hip) is probable for Monday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Initially questionable for Monday’s game, Barnes is trending toward being available. If cleared to play, he would take on his usual role in the Raptors’ lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Monday that Adou Thiero (knee) is ramping up his workouts and could return to game action by week’s end.
body: Thiero dealt with knee swelling at the end of preseason and has been unavailable since. That could change this week, as the second-year wing has recently ramped up his workout intensity. While this won’t affect fantasy basketball, Thiero’s return will add athleticism on the wing for the Lakers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland, Gradey Dick, Kris Dunn, Kobe Sanders and Brook Lopez will start Monday’s game against the Raptors.
body: The Clippers are down three starters for Monday’s game, with Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr. and Isaiah Jackson unavailable. They’ve been replaced in the lineup by Gradey, Sanders and Lopez. Of the three, Lopez may be the safest option for fantasy managers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Şengün will start Monday’s game against the Celtics.
body: VanVleet is back after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Thunder. As a result, Marcus Smart will head back to his customary bench role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alpha Diallo (wrist) is available for Monday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Diallo is back after a four-game absence. While his return adds wing depth for the Nuggets, it’s unlikely to affect fantasy basketball because Diallo will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg, Max Christie, Caleb Martin, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Monday’s game against the Kings.
body: The Mavericks won’t have Kyrie Irving for Monday’s game, which opens a spot in the starting lineup. Martin will fill the void, which raises his fantasy ceiling. However, that isn’t enough to make him a worthwhile streamer in most leagues, since there are 15 games on Monday’s schedule.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brayden Burries, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner will start against the Timberwolves on Monday.
body: Burries will get the first start of his career, with Ryan Rollins heading to the bench. There isn’t any injury reason for Rollins to head to the bench, so this could be a permanent move, which would bode well for Burries’ value.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kelly Oubre Jr. (knee) has been ruled out against the Hawks on Monday.
body: Oubre was never on the injury report, but he has been ruled out, with the update coming after the scheduled tipoff time. That will leave the Pacers with just six available players, which means those six will average out to 40 minutes of playing time.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: LaMelo Ball (wrist) is available for Monday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Despite a right wrist contusion, Ball is available to play on Monday. He’ll take on his usual role as the starting point guard, and the Timberwolves will need a more efficient Ball as they continue without Anthony Edwards (knee). He’s joined in the starting lineup by Ayo Dosunmu, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga and Rudy Gobert. Gobert’s return pushes Joan Beringer to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton will start against the Magic on Monday.
body: With Alex Sarr (ankle) sidelined, Ayton will get the starting nod at center. Ayton hasn’t been productive as a reserve this season, though this starting opportunity should allow him to have a solid outing.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is out for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Pippen will miss a second straight game after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Kings. His absence won’t significantly impact fantasy basketball, as Ty Jerome (back) is available. Javon Small could play a few minutes off the bench, but that isn’t guaranteed.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paul George (rest) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets.
body: The Celtics are playing the second leg of a back-to-back set, and PG will sit this one out. Baylor Scheierman and Sam Hauser are candidates to replace him in the starting five, though neither player is an appealing streamer with all 30 teams in action.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is doubtful for Monday’s matchup with the Kings.
body: Irving isn’t expected to play, which means Naji Marshall could replace him in the starting lineup. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on Irving’s status moving forward, as it’s unclear if this absence is serious or a maintenance day.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Dejounte Murray (personal) is listed as questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: Murray was off the injury report on Sunday, but he was added back on Monday afternoon, which puts his chances of playing in jeopardy. If Murray ends up sitting out, Herb Jones could remain in the starting lineup.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is available for Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: As expected, Murphy will suit up against Memphis, and fantasy managers should deploy him in lineups as usual.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: LaMelo Ball (wrist) and Terrence Shannon (hip) are questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Bucks.
body: With Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) sidelined, the Wolves’ backcourt could be thin on Monday. If Ball and/or Shannon sit out, more minutes would be available for Bones Hyland and Ayo Dosunmu.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Alex Sarr (knee) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Magic.
body: Sarr will sit out due to left knee soreness, which means Deandre Ayton should enter the starting lineup in his place.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Anthony Gill (back) has been ruled out for Monday’s matchup with Orlando.
body: Gill’s availability doesn’t impact fantasy hoops, as he’s not a part of Washington’s rotation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Hornets.
body: Joe will be out for at least one more game, which means Kevin Huerter and Ron Holland II should see increased run.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Pascal Siakam (rest) has been ruled out for Monday’s matchup with Atlanta.
body: Siakam will join the starters on the sideline, and he could be replaced in the first unit by Obi Toppin (back), who has been upgraded to questionable. Jay Huff should see big frontcourt minutes with Ivica Zubac (ankle) still on the shelf.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Aaron Nesmith (left hamstring injury management) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks.
body: Nesmith will get the night off on the second leg of a back-to-back set, as most of Indiana’s roster is on the injury report for this one. Fantasy managers looking for fill-in options can check the final injury report for availability, but with every team in action tonight, there are likely more attractive streamers.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Andrew Nembhard (cervical injury management) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks.
body: Nembhard will join most of Indiana’s roster on the sideline, as the Pacers punt on the second leg of a back-to-back set. Indiana has only seven players available on Monday, and Quenton Jackson should see heavy minutes as the biggest beneficiary of Nembhard’s absence.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.
body: Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick Jones Jr. (knee) finished Sunday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
body: Jones exited Sunday’s game late in the third quarter with a sore knee and did not return. That casts some doubt on his availability for Monday’s game against the Raptors. If Jones can’t play, Kobe Sanders may move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: Santos did not play in the second half of Sunday’s win over the Clippers, finishing with four points, three rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes. Following the victory, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that the team will re-evaluate Santos, whose knee tendinitis remains an issue. At a minimum, he’ll miss Monday’s game, which could mean more playing time for Georges Niang
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Immanuel Quickley accounted for 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Quickley has made at least three three-pointers in four straight and five of six games this season. That, along with the rebounds and assists, was the positive from his performance on Sunday. However, Quickley shot poorly against the Lakers, dropping his field-goal percentage to 37.6 percent for the season. It certainly isn’t impossible for a guard to provide solid value despite a low field-goal percentage, but fantasy managers want to see Quickley shoot better than he has.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: RJ Barrett accumulated 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Barrett has scored at least 20 points in three of his last four games, a stretch that coincides with the Raptors’ loss of Kawhi Leonard to a knee injury. While he didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, fantasy managers will be pleased with Barrett’s double-double, his first of the season, and the assists. The Raptors play three games next week, starting with the Clippers on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals.
body: Barnes’ mid-range mastery helped him score 29 points, and he’s scored at least 28 in three straight and four of his last five games. The exception was the October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, in which the Raptors’ star went scoreless. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) out for a few weeks, Barnes will need to shoulder more responsibility on both ends of the floor. And he’s shown the ability to do that in the past.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walker Kessler amassed 16 points (6-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 15 rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
body: A favorite of many fantasy managers willing to punt free-throw percentage, Kessler didn’t miss a shot from the field or the foul line on Sunday. Add in the rebounds and blocks, and this was a nice end to the week for those rostering the 7-footer. Kessler, who’s averaging just under three blocks per game, has blocked at least three shots in three games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves tallied 19 points (6-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
body: After committing eight turnovers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors, Reaves committed three against the Raptors. He didn’t shoot the ball particularly well on Sunday, but Reaves entered the game shooting 54.8 percent from the field and 42.4 percent from beyond the arc. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday when the Lakers host the Heat.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.
body: Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kris Dunn accumulated 12 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and seven steals in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: After failing to record a steal in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves, Dunn compensated with the best performance of his career. The seven steals mark a new career high for the former lottery pick, whose defense has made him a fixture in Tyronn Lue’s rotation since he joined the Clippers in 2024-25. Dunn also shot well on Sunday, but his defensive potential makes him an intriguing option for managers in 12-team leagues seeking steals.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kobe Sanders amassed 16 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Sanders had his most productive game of the season so far, setting new highs in points and three-pointers. He’s now played at least 20 minutes in four straight games, logging 30 against the Warriors. Sunday’s performance isn’t enough to get him on the radar in most fantasy leagues, but it may ensure Sanders a place in head coach Tyronn Lue’s rotation while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kingston Flemings has been suspended one game for his actions during Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
body: Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game after elbowing Pelicans wing Bryce McGowens in the face during a confrontation. The NBA has since suspended the rookie for one game, which he’ll serve on Monday against the Pacers. Flemings will be eligible to return on Wednesday against the Wizards.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is out for Sunday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Due to left shoulder bursitis, Poeltl is a late scratch for Sunday’s game. Trayce Jackson-Davis will replace him in the starting lineup, but Poeltl’s absence will likely give Collin Murray-Boyles more playing time as well.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski, Georges Niang, Yaxel Lendeborg and Charles Bassey will start Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: The Warriors are resting Stephen Curry and Draymond Green for Sunday’s game, prompting multiple changes to the starting lineup. Melton, Niang and Bassey will start, with Gui Santos coming off the bench after starting Friday’s win over the Lakers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Nembhard finished Sunday’s loss to the Nets with 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers.
body: Nembhard has scored at least 18 points in each of his last three games, all played without Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring). However, his efficiency has taken a hit, with Nembhard shooting 39.2 percent from the field and recording nine turnovers in those three outings. He’ll look to clean that up on Monday when the Pacers host the Hawks to begin a three-game week.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jay Huff missed both of his shot attempts in Sunday’s loss to the Nets, finishing with zero points and three rebounds.
body: It’s fair to say that Huff’s four starts for the injured Ivica Zubac (ankle) have not gone as well as many fantasy managers hoped. While he scored 13 points in Friday’s loss to the Heat, he has totaled 22 points, 16 rebounds and one block in those four games. Huff appeared to tweak his right foot in the first half of Sunday’s defeat but returned. Managers still holding onto him in hopes of getting some streaming value may be best served by moving on to another option going into Week 3.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Pascal Siakam tallied 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in Sunday’s loss to the Nets.
body: In the three games the Pacers have played since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam has averaged 18.7 points per game while shooting 45.8 percent from the field. That isn’t necessarily bad, but not sharing the floor with a lead guard as talented as Haliburton lowers Siakam’s ceiling. On Sunday, he scored just four points in the second half, shooting 1-of-3 from the field. The Pacers play three games next week, starting with the Hawks on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nolan Traoré accounted for 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: Having started the Nets’ last three games, Traoré’s production has been inconsistent. He rebounded nicely from a poor outing against the Pistons on Friday, scoring in double figures for the third time in four games. Traoré shot 4-of-8 from beyond the arc and committed one turnover in 30 minutes. Monday’s matchup against the Knicks will be more challenging, and Mikel Brown Jr. (back) should be available, which may limit Traoré’s ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Day’Ron Sharpe amassed 15 points (5-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: Playing against a Pacers team without Ivica Zubac or Obi Toppin, Sharpe had his most productive game of the season. The Nets center recorded his first double-double in six games, finishing with new highs in points and rebounds. Sharpe didn’t record any defensive stats, ending his two-game streak with at least one steal and one block. He’ll look to do more on that end of the floor on Monday when the Nets visit the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Julius Randle recorded 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: Despite shooting 1-of-6 from inside the arc, Randle finished Sunday’s victory with his third 20-point game of the season. Unfortunately for category league managers, Randle wasn’t efficient, shooting 33.3 percent from the field and committing four turnovers. That said, his performance against the Pacers was better than Friday’s showing against the Pistons.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Michael Porter Jr. tallied 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: The Nets got their first win of the season on Sunday, and getting Porter involved early helped. The Nets forward scored seven points in the first quarter and 13 in the first half. After attempting nine shots in Friday’s loss to the Pistons, Porter nearly matched that number in the first quarter (seven). He’ll need to take a similar approach on Monday when the Nets begin a four-game week with a matchup with the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is available for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Santos is good to go after being listed as probable on the initial injury report. While he may start, it isn’t guaranteed that Santos will get the minutes needed to affect fantasy basketball. He most recently played 16 minutes in Friday’s win over the Lakers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Sunday that Ziaire Williams (foot) is dealing with soreness, so he’s sitting out Sunday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Sunday’s game will be the third Williams has missed due to left foot/heel injury management. The good news is that, while Williams is dealing with soreness, scans of the foot came back clean. Jake LaRavia should remain in the starting lineup until Williams is cleared to return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine (elbow) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: LaVine is dealing with right elbow inflammation. He hasn’t missed a game this season, but if that changes, Malik Monk could take on a bigger role, whether he starts or comes off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is doubtful for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Pippen did not play in Saturday’s win over the Kings and appears likely to remain out on Monday. Ty Jerome (back) is available, so Pippen remaining out would not put the Grizzlies in a terrible spot. Javon Small could play some off the bench after logging 20 minutes on Saturday, but that isn’t guaranteed.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome (back) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Jerome is back after sitting out Saturday’s win against the Kings. As a result, Cam Spencer will return to the bench after dishing out 13 assists in the spot start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Franz Wagner tallied 14 points (5-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: While Wagner set a career high with 12 assists, he struggled to make shots. Shooting 54.2 percent from inside the arc entering Sunday, the Magic forward shot 4-of-16 from inside the arc against the Celtics. Wagner is shooting 39.6 percent for the season, but three-point shooting has been the issue (18.5 percent entering Sunday). He’ll look to turn things around on Monday against the Wizards.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Black recorded 23 points (6-of-12 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Black has reached double figures in three of his four games this season, and Sunday’s point total is a new season-high. The overall stat line was very good, with the Magic guard shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line and offering solid value in rebounds and steals. Black will continue to start until Paolo Banchero (ankle) returns, making him worth adding if he’s still on your league’s waiver wire.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Desmond Bane accumulated 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: For the second straight game, Bane made at least five three-pointers, shooting 5-of-9 against the Celtics. The Magic guard shot over 50 percent from the field on Sunday, a sign he’s warming up after a slow start. Bane is shooting 36.9 percent from the field through six games, far below his career mark of 47.3 percent. Orlando begins a three-game Week 3 on Monday against the Wizards.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Neemias Queta produced eight points (4-of-9 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
body: Mitchell Robinson (rest) did not play in the first game of Boston’s road back-to-back, so Queta started at center. While he didn’t offer much scoring, the 7-footer was effective on the glass and as a rim protector. On offense, the Celtics got solid contributions from Luka Garza, who finished with 10 points, two rebounds, one assist, and two three-pointers. Boston visits Houston on Monday, and Robinson should return to the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Monday’s game will be the third that Caruso has missed since spraining his right ankle during Oklahoma City’s October 26 win over the Suns. Injuries have forced the Thunder to go deep into their bench, with rookie Bennett Stirtz playing 25 minutes or more in each of the last three games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is out for Monday’s game against the Pistons.
body: While Knueppel is close to making his season debut, he isn’t ready yet. Sion James is likely to remain in the starting lineup until last season’s Rookie of the Year runner-up is cleared to play without restrictions.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Coby White (calf) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Pistons.
body: Injured just before the preseason began, White is available to make his season debut on Monday. Given the time he missed, he’ll likely have a minutes restriction. Dennis Schröder has served as the starting point guard, but that may change once White is up to speed.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Since taking a hard fall during an October 25 win over the Pistons, Joe has missed the last three games with a hip contusion. If he remains out, Kevin Huerter and Ronald Holland II may once again be asked to fill out the wing rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: LeBron is back after missing Saturday’s win over the Hornets, the second game of a back-to-back. Who he pushes to the bench may depend on Joel Embiid (foot), who is questionable. If Embiid can play, Dean Wade would head to the bench. If Embiid can’t play, the 76ers could go without a true center, starting LeBron and Wade together, with Adem Bona on the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid (foot) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Embiid did not play in Saturday’s win over the Hornets, as it was Philadelphia’s second game in as many nights. The 7-footer remains on the injury report, which is concerning, but the 76ers would likely rather their former MVP miss games now than later in the season. Adem Bona started on Saturday, but the 76ers were also without LeBron James. With LeBron off the injury report, Bona could be headed to the bench regardless of what happens with Embiid.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is out for Monday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Landale strained his left hip early in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans and did not return. Asa Newell moved into the backup center role and may do the same on Monday. Newell should only be rostered in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Johnson (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Johnson had to leave Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans after the third quarter with a sprained left ankle. If he can’t play Monday, Aaron Wiggins could move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Peyton Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Watson has not missed a game this season, but that could change on Monday due to a sore right hamstring. If he can’t play, Mario Hezonja or Meleek Thomas could replace him in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Tyson remains out for a second straight game as he recovers from a right ankle sprain. Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor absorbed some of the minutes Tyson would have played if he’d been healthy for Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Obi Toppin (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: While Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said Toppin won’t play Sunday, he left the door open for the forward to play Monday against the Hawks. Kobe Brown played 20 minutes off the bench in Friday’s loss to the Heat and may take on a similar workload against the Nets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Hugo González has replaced Jordan Walsh in the starting lineup for Sunday’s game against the Magic.
body: The Celtics’ initial starting lineup had just one replacement: Neemias Queta for Mitchell Robinson (rest). However, González has replaced Walsh, who will be available off the bench. Derrick White, Paul George and Jayson Tatum complete the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan Poole (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Poole will miss a third consecutive game with left ankle tendinopathy. Bryce McGowens has played rotation minutes off the bench recently and should continue to do so, but he’s unlikely to offer reliable fantasy value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is probable for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: The probable tag suggests that Murphy will ultimately be available for Monday’s game. If he can’t play, Herb Jones may remain in the starting lineup, since Dejounte Murray (personal) is available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dejounte Murray (personal) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Murray will be available on Monday after missing the last two games for personal reasons. His return likely means that Herb Jones will head to the bench, and it may also lower Jeremiah Fears’ fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta will start Sunday’s game against the Magic.
body: Sunday’s game is the first of two in as many days for the Celtics, who visit the Rockets on Monday. As a result, Mitchell Robinson (rest) will sit, and Queta will replace him in the starting lineup. Luka Garza should pick up additional minutes off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: According to Knicks head coach Mike Brown, Jose Alvarado (ankle) participated in Sunday’s practice.
body: Alvarado has missed the Knicks’ last four games with a sprained ankle, resulting in Tyler Kolek entering the rotation. While he did play well in the first three games that Alvarado missed, Kolek struggled in Friday’s loss to the 76ers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tim Hardaway Jr. (personal) missed Heat practice on Sunday but is expected to rejoin the team in time for Monday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Hardaway has come off the bench in each of Miami’s first six games, averaging 6.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.0 three-pointers in 18.2 minutes. His production hasn’t been enough to merit a roster spot in fantasy leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: According to Bulls head coach Tiago Splitter, Nic Claxton (hamstring) fully participated in Sunday’s practice.
body: Acquired from the Nets in a multi-team trade this summer, Claxton strained his hamstring in early October and has been out since. However, his Bulls debut may not be far away, as he practiced on Sunday without limitations. Jalen Smith has been the starting center in Claxton’s absence, and managers may want to hold onto him until Claxton can play with no restrictions on his playing time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Vit Krejčí finished Saturday’s win over the Jazz with five points (2-of-6 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: With Saturday’s game being Portland’s first since losing Ja Morant to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, head coach Micah Nori had to alter his rotation. One change was more playing time for Krejčí, who logged 24 minutes in the 112-90 victory. His production wasn’t enough to make him a player worth adding going into Week 3, but Krejčí should get more opportunities in the coming weeks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (rest) is out for Sunday’s game against the Magic.
body: Boston plays on Sunday and Monday, so Robinson sitting is not a major surprise. Neemias Queta is the most likely replacement in the starting lineup, and Luka Garza’s playing time is likely to increase.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kenrich Williams finished Saturday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers.
body: After totaling 10 points in his first two starts of the season, Williams scored 11 on Saturday. He was most valuable against the Rockets in three-pointers and rebounds, but this performance doesn’t make “Kenny Hustle” a must-add heading into Oklahoma City’s four-game Week 3. Also, with the Thunder playing two games against Cleveland to start the week, it’s fair to wonder whether head coach Mark Daigneault would consider a bigger lineup to match up with Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. If so, Williams or Jared McCain (10/4/2/1) could be headed to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Hartenstein amassed 10 points (3-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and three steals in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets.
body: With Chet Holmgren (knee) out for at least 8-10 weeks, the Thunder will rely even more on Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams (3/4/1/1) and Aday Mara (seven points, nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks) in the post. Of the three, Hartenstein is the safest option for fantasy managers, which is why he’s rostered in over 80 percent of Yahoo leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 26 points (10-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets.
body: Since the October 25 game against the Clippers in which Oklahoma City lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, Gilgeous-Alexander has shot 49.1 percent from the field and 5-of-17 from beyond the arc. Of course, the Thunder have also lost Chet Holmgren since last Sunday, which allows opposing teams to devote even more attention to slowing down SGA. Fantasy managers will hope his efficiency doesn’t take too big a hit in the weeks to come. Oklahoma City plays four games next week, starting with two against the Cavaliers on Monday (away) and Wednesday (home).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alperen Şengün finished Saturday’s win over the Thunder with 16 points (6-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds, nine assists and one block.
body: Şengün returned to the Rockets lineup after sitting out Friday’s loss to the Mavericks with a sore back. He played 33 minutes and finished one rebound and one assist shy of a triple-double. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün at times, but he’s gotten off to a good start this season. Clint Capela, who started on Friday, recorded four rebounds and two assists in 10 minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Marcus Smart accumulated 24 points (7-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Smart started Saturday night, as the Rockets did not have Fred VanVleet (knee) due to injury management. The veteran guard shot 7-of-10 from beyond the arc against the Thunder and recorded his first regular-season 20-point game since March 14 against the Nuggets, when he played for the Lakers. While Smart will be a fixture in the Rockets’ rotation, his fantasy outlook hinges on VanVleet’s availability.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jabari Smith Jr. produced 30 points (10-of-18 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, five assists, one block and six three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Smith matched his season high with 30 points, recording the seventh 30-point game of his NBA career on Saturday. Against the Thunder, he shot 6-of-12 from three, helping the Rockets compensate for Fred VanVleet’s absence and a relatively quiet night from Kevin Durant (14/3/4/1/3). Smith has gotten off to an excellent start, leaving some to decide whether to “sell high” or bet he continues to play this well. The Rockets play three games next week, starting with the Celtics on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis recorded 11 points (3-of-5 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 14 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: Fantasy managers rostering Sabonis received solid returns in rebounds and assists. However, the Kings center took just five shots on Saturday, matching his season low. Sabonis is averaging 9.2 attempts per game, his fewest since 2018-19. Zach LaVine (11 points, one assist) attempted nine shots on Saturday. With rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. having the ultimate “green light,” it will be interesting to see how vets like Sabonis and LaVine adjust.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter amassed 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
body: While Hunter’s streak of 20-point games didn’t reach three on Saturday, he did hit double digits in shot attempts for the third straight game. His fantasy value has been limited for most of his career, especially in category leagues, because he hasn’t produced much in assists, steals, or blocks. However, Hunter’s recent scoring run and Keegan Murray’s continued absence make him someone to consider adding in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. finished Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies with 38 points (12-of-25 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and nine three-pointers.
body: After six games, it’s clear the Kings won’t impose any offensive limitations on Acuff. While efficiency can be an issue at times, that was not the case on Saturday. Acuff established new highs in points and three-pointers while shooting a respectable 48 percent from the field. He was especially good in the first half, scoring 21 points on 7-of-13 shooting and committing one turnover. The Kings play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: GG Jackson recorded 21 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
body: Jackson entered Saturday having made four of 13 three-point attempts over five games. Going 5-of-5 as he did against the Kings will give the three-point percentage a welcome boost, all the way up to 50 percent. Scoring in double figures for the third time in six games, Jackson also posted a season-high 21 points against the Kings. He still isn’t worth fully committing to in most fantasy leagues. However, GG may be worth considering in certain matchups, especially on nights when the Grizzlies are down a key scorer (Ty Jerome didn’t play on Saturday).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyle Kuzma amassed 14 points (6-of-12 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
body: Kuzma’s shot 50 percent or better from the field in four of his last five appearances, solid efficiency for a player who hasn’t been known for that in the past. However, the overall stat line probably wasn’t enough to convince managers in 12-team leagues to consider adding Kuzma. The Bucks open a four-game Week 3 on Monday against the Timberwolves.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Myles Turner produced 10 points (4-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
body: Turner had his hands full with Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, who combined for 52 points and 16 rebounds. Milwaukee’s veteran center recorded a complete stat line, but the value was a bit limited beyond the rebounds and blocks. Kel’el Ware (19/10/3/1/2 with three-pointers) finished with a better stat line, but he played 12 of his 24 minutes in the fourth quarter after the outcome was no longer in doubt.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro finished Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers with 15 points (5-of-18 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
body: This wasn’t Herro’s best night, as he shot 1-of-7 from inside the arc. While the four three-pointers will please some fantasy managers, the overall output was disappointing. However, given the gap between the Bucks and Cavaliers, it wasn’t all that surprising. Herro will look to bounce back on Monday when the Bucks visit the Timberwolves. Milwaukee plays four games next week.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: James Harden accumulated 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
body: With the Cavaliers getting dominant efforts from Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, they didn’t need much from Harden or Donovan Mitchell (15/4/3 with two three-pointers) on Saturday. However, fantasy managers rostering either guard likely hoped for more production. Harden played 26 minutes on Saturday, checking out for the last time with 2:45 remaining in the third quarter.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jarrett Allen tallied 25 points (12-of-16 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
body: Not only did Allen record his first double-double of the season on Saturday, but the 25 points were a season-high for the Cavaliers’ center. He scored 19 of his 25 points in the first half, shooting 9-of-12 from the field. Shooting 65.5 percent from the field thus far, Allen has provided greater value than many fantasy managers expected before the season began.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Evan Mobley finished Saturday’s win over the Bucks with 27 points (11-of-16 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
body: Cleveland removed most of the drama from Saturday’s game with a 48-point second quarter, led by Mobley. Shooting 5-of-5 from the field, he scored 13 points in the quarter, and frontcourt sidekick Jarrett Allen added nine. Mobley played just one minute in the fourth quarter, or his stat line could have been more robust. The Cavaliers play four games next week, starting with the undermanned Thunder on Monday (home) and Wednesday (away).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nickeil Alexander-Walker accounted for 12 points (3-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
body: Alexander-Walker had a rough night in New Orleans, missing all six of his three-point attempts. As a result, his streak of five straight games with at least two three-pointers to begin the season ended. Add in the lackluster assist and steal production, and this was a tough night for fantasy managers rostering Alexander-Walker. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday against the Pacers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Johnson (ankle) recorded 13 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
body: Johnson played the entire third quarter, but that would be the last we’d see of him on the court Saturday night. The Hawks forward sprained his left ankle, and while Johnson was questionable to return, he didn’t, as the game got out of hand. Atlanta’s four-game Week 3 begins on Monday against the Pacers and includes a back-to-back. If Johnson misses time, Aaron Wiggins (10/2/1/1/1 with two three-pointers) could become more important.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: CJ McCollum finished Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans with 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: Playing in New Orleans for the first time since he was traded to Washington in the summer of 2025, McCollum had a relatively quiet Saturday night. The field-goal percentage was good, but CJ’s overall stat line was a bit lean. The Hawks lost Jalen Johnson to a sprained ankle in the second half, and McCollum may be needed to produce more offensively if the star forward misses time. Atlanta plays four games next week, starting with Indiana on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zion Williamson accumulated 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, four assists and three steals in Saturday’s win over the Hawks.
body: While Williamson’s defensive effort has been questioned at times, he’s provided consistent value in steals this season. He’s had at least two in each of the Pelicans’ first six games and is averaging 3.2 per game. His most productive season was 2024-25, when Zion averaged 1.2 steals per game. This early production is definitely out of the norm for him, so fantasy managers should plan for a likely decrease at some point.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) will not return to Saturday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Landale played just over one minute before exiting Saturday’s game in the first quarter with a left hip injury. Asa Newell has entered the rotation off the bench and could retain that role if Landale misses time beyond Saturday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ziaire Williams (foot) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Williams has missed the Lakers’ last two games, so Jake LaRavia has moved into the starting lineup. If Williams remains out, LaRavia will get another start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Carr (oblique) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Carr, who suffered a strained oblique during the preseason, will be available to make his NBA debut on Sunday. How much he plays remains to be seen, especially with the Lakers also playing on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is questionable to return to Saturday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Landale played for one minute before leaving Saturday’s game with a left hip injury. If he can’t return, Asa Newell will likely play rotation minutes off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball, Ayo Dosunmu, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga and Joan Beringer will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Rudy Gobert is out with lower back spasms, so Beringer will make his first start of the season. While this is an incredibly challenging matchup for the second-year center, he’s worth the streaming risk in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: The Grizzlies are without Ty Jerome, who’s out with a back injury. Spencer will start at point guard, and with Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) also out, he’ll likely log heavy minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: The Grizzlies will be without two rotation guards on Saturday, as Pippen and Ty Jerome (back) are out. Cam Spencer will play more minutes and is worth streaming in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: Jerome will miss a game for the first time this season. His absence likely means Cam Spencer will start, especially with Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) also out. Spence is worth streaming due to the absences.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Meleek Thomas (foot) is available for Saturday’s game against the Bucks.
body: A few hours after being upgraded from questionable to probable, Thomas is available for Saturday’s game. He’ll take on the bench role he filled in his first two appearances, averaging 13.0 points per game.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said Saturday that the team is being “very, very methodical” in the handling of Tobias Harris’ (calf) rehab.
body: Harris, whom the Spurs signed to a two-year deal in July, has not yet played because of a strained calf suffered during training camp. Based on Johnson’s pregame comments on Saturday, the veteran forward may not take the court for some time. “We need to just be patient and make sure we get it all the way right and get him all the way right in terms of being ready to prepare to play an NBA game at the (fast-paced) style of play we want,” Johnson said. Until then, the Spurs may not make any changes to their starting lineup as long as the current starters are healthy.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephon Castle (migraine) is available for Saturday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Castle is available after initially being listed as questionable for Saturday’s game. He’ll occupy his usual place in the Spurs’ starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Marcus Smart, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Şengün will start Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: While Şengün is back in the lineup after missing Friday’s loss to the Mavericks, Fred VanVleet (knee) is out for injury management. Smart will slide into the starting point guard role, while Şengün’s return pushes Clint Capela to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Al Horford (back) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Horford has not played both games of a back-to-back in a few years. So his absence from the injury report for Sunday’s game means he’s unlikely to play Monday against the Suns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Obi Toppin (back) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: Toppin sat out Friday’s loss to the Heat, leading to Kobe Brown joining the rotation and playing 20 minutes off the bench. If Toppin plays Sunday, Brown is likely to slide out of the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Nets.
body: Nesmith is probable for Sunday, which should bode well for his chances of playing. However, it’s the first of two games in as many days for the Pacers. If Nesmith plays against the Nets, fantasy managers should plan for the possibility that he sits on Monday against the Hawks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mikel Brown Jr. (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Brown, who missed time with a sprained ankle, hasn’t reached the point where the Nets feel comfortable with him playing back-to-backs. He’ll sit on Sunday and should be available for Monday’s game against the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (rest) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Magic.
body: Robinson is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Magic. If he’s ultimately ruled out, Neemias Queta is a candidate to start and could be worth streaming.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Santos sat out Wednesday’s win over the Timberwolves due to left knee tendinitis. He started Friday against the Lakers but logged just 16 minutes. Santos is on track to play Sunday, and with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green out, he may be asked to take on a larger role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Draymond Green (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Green is going to sit out Sunday with lower back injury management. Georges Niang will likely move into the starting lineup with Green absent.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Stephen Curry (knee) is out for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Curry is going to sit out Sunday for right knee injury management reasons. Will Richard is likely the top candidate to move into the starting lineup with Curry sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Stephon Castle (migraine) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Castle popped up on the injury report Saturday as questionable with a migraine. With Castle potentially on the wrong side of questionable, Julian Champagnie is a candidate to enter the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Ace Bailey, Lauri Makkanen and Jaxson Hayes against the Trail Blazers on Saturday.
body: Markkanen missed Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with a wrist injury, but is set to return Saturday against the Trail Blazers. Josh Green will head back to the bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Meleek Thomas (foot) is probable for Saturday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Thomas missed Thursday’s loss to the Hawks, but is trending in the right direction for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. He’ll have a role off the bench if he’s available.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is available for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Markkanen missed Wednesday’s game against the Spurs with a sprained right wrist. He’ll return Saturday against the Trail Blazers, likely sending Josh Green back to the bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Robert Williams (knee) is available for Saturday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Williams is available after missing Thursday’s loss to the Grizzlies. He doesn’t have much fantasy value at this point in his career on a crowded Trail Blazers bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Rudy Gobert (back) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Gobert is questionable with low back spasms. Joan Beringer had 12 points, seven rebounds and two blocks against the Cavaliers earlier this week and would likely start if Gobert is ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Reed Sheppard (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Sheppard is out again with a back injury. With Fred VanVleet (knee) also out, expect Marcus Smart to move into the starting lineup while Bogdan Bogdanovic should also see a boost in minutes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Fred VanVleet (knee) is out for Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: VanVleet will sit with right knee injury management and it likely won’t be the last time he does so this season. With Reed Sheppard (back) also out, Marcus Smart should move into the starting lineup Saturday against the Thunder.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Alperen Şengün (back) is off the injury report ahead of Saturday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Şengün is good to go after sitting out Friday’s game against the Mavericks with back soreness. He should be started in all formats. Clint Capela will head back to the bench after picking up a spot start Friday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jabari Walker (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Walker has missed the last three games with a knee injury. If he’s out again, Adem Bona should start and see plenty of minutes with Joel Embiid (foot) also out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylen Brown (knee) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Brown missed Friday’s win over the Knicks, which was his first absence of the year. He’s questionable for Saturday’s game against the Hornets with a knee injury. If he’s out again, Dean Wade could move into the starting lineup just as he did Friday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Joel Embiid (foot) is out for Saturday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Embiid had a 10/7/7 line in Friday’s win over the Knicks, but he’ll sit out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back. With Embiid out, Adem Bona and Jabari Walker are candidates to move into the startling lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: LeBron James (sciatica) is out for Saturday’s game against the Hornets.
body: James posted as 20/9/8 line in Friday’s win over the Knicks, but he’ll sit out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back. At age-41, LeBron isn’t going to play every night, but fantasy managers knew that going into the season.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports the Thunder are no longer signing Ochai Agbaji in light of Chet Holmgren’s injury.
body: Agbaji was waived by the Knicks earlier this month. Charania reported Friday that he was signed by the Thunder, but Oklahoma City is re-evaluating its open roster spot in light of losing Holmgren (knee) for at least two months. It appears Agbaji will have to catch on with another team.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Walker Kessler finished Friday’s loss to the Warriors with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 13 rebounds, two assists and five blocks.
body: Kessler has blocked at least five shots in two games this season and at least one in each of the Lakers’ six games. Add in the rebounds and field-goal percentage, and this was a good night for fantasy managers who are rostering the 7-footer. As long as Kessler can stay healthy, he should provide good value for those punting free-throw percentage. The Lakers end their week with a home game against the Raptors on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves accounted for 21 points (9-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Although Reaves recorded his fifth 20-point game in six appearances, it was not a good night for him. For those hoping Luka Dončić’s return to the Lakers’ lineup would help limit Reaves’ turnovers, he committed eight for the second straight game. He was also 1-of-6 from three, but the recent jump in turnovers is a concern, especially for managers in nine-cat leagues. Hopefully, Reaves will take better care of the basketball on Sunday against the Raptors.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić accumulated 37 points (12-of-27 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, two blocks and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Dončić was rolling during the first quarter, knocking down five three-pointers and scoring 21 points. Unfortunately for the Lakers, their star guard needed a rest to start the second quarter, which opened the door for the Warriors to turn things around. While Dončić scored 13 second-half points, he didn’t get enough help from teammates beyond Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler to avoid the defeat. The Lakers host Toronto on Sunday to end their week.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski tallied 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Lakers.
body: After taking a back seat offensively in Wednesday’s win over the Timberwolves, Podziemski was more involved on Friday to make up for a quiet night from Yaxel Lendeborg (six points, one rebound, one three-pointer, and five turnovers). Podz scored 14 of his 21 points in the second half, shooting 4-of-8 from the field and 3-of-4 from the foul line. The 21 points are a season-high for Podziemski, who scored 18 in each of his first two appearances.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Anthony Melton produced 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Lakers.
body: Golden State’s bench made the difference on Friday, outscoring the Lakers’ bench 47-4. Melton scored 13 of his 16 points in the second quarter, shooting 3-of-4 from beyond the arc. He needed just 21 minutes to record his final stat line, showing why Melton can add value for category-league managers despite coming off the bench. The Warriors play one more game this week, hosting the Clippers on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry finished Friday’s win over the Lakers with 31 points (11-of-23 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers.
body: The Warriors got off to a terribly slow start, being outscored 38-15 in the first quarter. The bench came up big in the second quarter, setting the stage for Curry to do his usual work in the second half. He scored 17 of his 31 after halftime, helping the Warriors turn a 25-point deficit into a 17-point victory. During the third quarter, Curry moved into 18th on the NBA’s all-time scoring list, passing Dominique Wilkins. Over the last two games, he’s scored 75 points and knocked down 14 three-pointers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokic put up 18 points (8-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, ten assists, three steals, and five turnovers on Friday.
body: While it’s not the best performance from Jokic with his standards, it’s still a very good performance. He will have games where he’s not the most aggressive at scoring the ball and tonight was one of those. Jokic is 31 years old, so there might be some regression coming at some point down the road. For now, sit back and enjoy the ride with one of the most unique players in NBA history.
